jp: {もし|av-moshi}母[はは]が先[さき]に帰[かえ]ってきたら、夕飯[ゆうはん]の準備[じゅんび]を始[はじ]めておいてくれますか。
en: If Mother gets home first, could you start getting dinner ready?
why: もし opens an ordinary if-clause closed by たら; たとえ would need ても and きっと cannot start a clause.

jp: {万一[まんいち]/もし|av-moshi}子[こ]どもが夜中[よなか]に熱[ねつ]を出[だ]したら、すぐ救急[きゅうきゅう]病院[びょういん]に連[つ]れて行[い]きます。
en: If, by any chance, our child runs a fever in the middle of the night, I will take them straight to the emergency hospital.
why: 万一 marks an unlikely, unwelcome possibility and goes with たら; たとえ would demand ても.

jp: もし弟[おとうと]が早[はや]く{起[お]きれば/起[お]きたら|av-moshi}、朝[あさ]ごはんを一緒[いっしょ]に食[た]べられるのに。
en: If my little brother got up early, we could have breakfast together.
why: もし calls for a conditional ending; 起きても would mean "even if he gets up", which kills the wish.

jp: もし祖母[そぼ]が{元気[げんき]だったら/元気[げんき]なら|av-moshi}、今年[ことし]も一緒[いっしょ]に旅行[りょこう]できたのに。
en: If my grandmother were well, we could have travelled together this year too.
why: もし is completed by a conditional; 元気でも means "even if", and ので / のに state a fact, which contradicts できたのに.

jp: {仮[かり]に/もし|av-moshi}家賃[やちん]が今[いま]の半分[はんぶん]なら、もっと広[ひろ]い部屋[へや]に住[す]めるのに。
en: Supposing the rent were half what it is now, I could live in a bigger room.
why: 仮に sets up an imagined case with なら; たとえ would need ても.

jp: もし赤[あか]ちゃんが夜[よる]に{泣[な]いたら|av-moshi}、私[わたし]が起[お]きてミルクをあげます。
en: If the baby cries in the night, I will get up and give it milk.
why: もし goes with a conditional; 泣いても ("even if"), ので and のに do not give the "if" the promise needs.
